LESSON: READING 1.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: School Suggested vocabulary bell, lesson, chalkboard, chalk, books, block, bag, 
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 1.2.1 Fluency, part of School Suggested vocabulary bell, lesson, chalkboard, chalk, books, block, bag,  in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read at the right speed? 2. Why should we read a text accurately?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch/listen to an audio visual clip/ listen to an audio recording/teacher model of the target sounds

2. Pick out words targeting the letter sound combinations- bl, sp, sc, sk, ck

3. Practice sitting in the appropriate posture, hold the book in the right position and turn the pages carefully while reading.

4. Read short texts observing stress and intonation 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch/listen to an audio visual clip/ listen to an audio recording/teacher model of the target sounds
2. Pick out words targeting the letter sound combinations- bl, sp, sc, sk, ck
3. Practice sitting in the appropriate posture, hold the book in the right position and turn the pages carefully while reading.
4. Read short texts observing stress and intonation 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Leaning to learn: The learner’s ability to learn independently is enhanced as the practice reading texts at the right speed, expressively and

accurately on their own.

• Communication and Collaboration: Teamwork is enhanced as the learner actively takes part in the discussion.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: A learner interacts with the text and answers direct and indirect questions using contextual clues.

Values:
• Responsibility is enhanced as the learner takes care of books while holding them in the right position and turning the pages carefully while

reading.

• Unity: A learner works in pairs to identify sentences containing answers to direct questions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Life skills: -Self-awareness is enhanced as the learner becomes aware of the appropriate posture during reading.

• Self-esteem is nurtured as they acquire reading fluency skills

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies reading fluency skills acquired when reading texts in Kiswahili and Indigenous language activities
